Why is there no overall rating yet?
Mapped canopy

Road proximity is not a noise reading and may be an advantage for access, so it does not reduce any livability rating. We show tree cover as a separate observation. A defensible 5-star overall rating would need validated inputs for actual sound, transport, dwelling conditions, safety, heat and other factors. We do not give made-up stars.

NSW EPA notifications are shown separately for human review; they cannot be converted into a contamination risk score.

THE EVIDENCE LEDGER · THREE SOURCES

Know what the map knows.

The atlas no longer turns road separation into a livability penalty or claims measured sound. Canopy, road geometry and EPA records are distinct observations; an overall property rating is withheld until there is enough relevant and validated evidence.

●
Source data

Road centreline geometry from NSW Spatial Services, a government spatial dataset. Snapshot metadata loading…

◐
Derived here

Shortest distance to road centreline and total mapped line length inside the 200 m circle. Approximate planar geometry, rounded for display.

●
Nearby traffic counter observations

Where present, published national Harmonised Traffic Counts records identify the counting station, measured vehicle count and year. The counter may be far away, on a different road, or cover only part of a year; it is never treated as sound measured at the selected point.

○
Not observed at this home

Sound pressure (dB), true nighttime traffic levels at the address, aircraft and railway exposure, façades, indoor conditions and bedroom-side sound remain unknown.

Inspect the original NSW feature layer ↗

Visible on map

Other sources in development
Use responsibly: These are measurements on a road map, not measurements of sound. A nearby road need not be loud; a distant railway, flight path, venue or neighbour may be. Never infer indoor quietness from this alone.
Calculation details

At the selected coordinates, we calculate perpendicular distances to mapped road-centreline segments in a local planar approximation. We display the shortest distance, rounded to the nearest metre. The 200 m road-length figure clips each line segment against a circle of radius 200 m and sums the portions inside. Duplicate road geometries appearing in multiple source tiles are removed first.

Results depend on the completeness and precision of the road geometry. The NSW snapshot is dated, may omit local roads, and does not provide traffic intensity or sound levels. The 200 m length is suppressed close to the snapshot's boundary. Alternate live sources can vary in coverage and classification.

How the colourful direction model works

Road segments within 250 m of the selected point are sampled at regular intervals. Each sample contributes to a compass direction, weighted down with distance. Twelve relative directional wedges are drawn at different heights. Tall, warm-coloured sectors have more nearby mapped road geometry in this particular circle; they do not indicate actual acoustic direction or decibels. At close zoom the diagram shrinks in screen-space, so its visible radius is not a geographic boundary. Its very gentle pulse is decorative, not live traffic.

The optional imagery basemap comes from NSW Spatial Services' public aerial and satellite imagery mosaic. Photography dates vary by neighbourhood. Imagery © NSW Department of Customer Service; mosaic includes third-party imagery © AAM, Jacobs Group Ausimage and LANDSAT.

Can I use this to choose an apartment?

Use it only to shortlist areas to investigate. Window glazing, floor height, apartment orientation, neighbours, ventilation, construction, and late-night businesses can dominate indoor noise. Visit candidate homes during the hours you care about and check bedroom-side sound conditions.

●
NSW 2024–25 canopy access

NSW Government's hexagonal canopy dataset from aerial imagery acquired between 12 Dec 2024 and 5 Apr 2025. Trees taller than 3 m count as canopy. Each small hexagon reports its own canopy proportion, not a suburb average.

◐
Mapped here

The actual hexagons around the selected point are coloured by their recorded canopy proportion. The ring displays the proportion of the selected hexagon, not a temperature estimate.

●
Individual trees and terrain

In 3D, a subset of registered park and street trees within the City of Sydney LGA uses City of Sydney's published locations, heights and north–south canopy spreads. The foliage and trunk shapes are schematic: they are not surveyed crowns or branch structures. Other council areas, including Kensington, have no equivalent individual tree layer yet. 3D ground relief uses Mapterhorn terrain tiles from various publicly documented elevation datasets (resolution differs by area), separately from the NSW Spatial Services 5 m DEM height queried at the selected point. Neither model captures rooftop or garden contours; tree heights are from the council asset register, not remeasured here.

☀
Sun position and modelled building shadows

Solar azimuth and elevation are calculated from Sydney local date/time and selected coordinates using NOAA-style solar geometry. In 3D, shadow polygons are projected onto an assumed level ground plane from OpenStreetMap-derived building footprints and render heights when available. Sun-facing extrusion lighting changes with time. Shadows are not terrain-aware; trees, missing buildings and overhangs are omitted. This is a neighbourhood illustration, not a property-level shadow study.

○
Not measured here

Air temperature, land surface temperature, heat exposure indoors, the number of extreme-heat days and real-time conditions are not included. Missing cells remain uncoloured.

●
NSW EPA notifications

Sites notified as potentially contaminated under the Contaminated Land Management Act. Records have names, addresses, activities and management classes, which can differ substantially.

◐
Mapped here

We count point records up to 1 km from your chosen location, calculate approximate straight-line distances and show the nearest record's published management class. A point is not the actual affected parcel boundary.

○
Not established

Soil testing at your address, contamination extent, current exposure pathways, site safety and completeness of the register. A zero result does not mean a verified clean site.
